summary: Find every non-canonical document that contradicts the 2026 travel and expense policy or the remote work policy; a good answer lists the 11 drifted statements with file, wrong text and the canonical rule, and does not report stricter department rules, dated superseded emails, contractor terms or other decoys.

findings.what: Handbook section 7 gives the old meals per diem of $55 per day; canonical is $65 ($85 high-cost).

evidence.quote: you receive a meals and incidentals allowance of $55 per day while traveling
| Standard locations | $65 |

findings.counts_if: Names handbook section 7 (travel and business expenses) as stating a $55 per diem where policy says $65.

findings.what: HR FAQ says receipts are only needed for expenses over $50; canonical requires an itemized receipt for any expense of $30 or more.

evidence.quote: You only need to keep receipts for expenses over $50.
An itemized receipt is required for any single expense of $30 or more.

findings.counts_if: Names the HR FAQ receipt answer ($50) as conflicting with the $30 receipt threshold.

findings.what: Manager guide says employees have 60 days to submit expense reports; canonical deadline is 30 calendar days.

evidence.quote: Employees have 60 days from the end of a trip to submit their report in Clearline
Submit expense reports in Clearline within 30 calendar days after the end of the trip

findings.counts_if: Names the manager guide's 60-day submission window as conflicting with the 30-day deadline.

findings.what: Member Services wiki lets team leads and supervisors approve reports up to $1,000 alone; canonical allows a manager alone only up to $500, and a department may not set more generous rules.

evidence.quote: **Team leads and supervisors can approve reports up to $1,000 on their own.**
| Up to $500 | Direct manager |

findings.counts_if: Names the Member Services $1,000 single-approver limit as drift (more generous than the $500 manager limit), not as an allowed departmental rule.

findings.what: Handbook Appendix C lists the Connectivity Allowance as $75 per month (the rejected proposal); canonical stipend is $50 per month. Handbook section 9 points to Appendix C for the amount.

evidence.quote: | Connectivity Allowance | Employees with an approved hybrid or fully remote arrangement | $75 per month |
See Appendix C for the current amount.
receive a connectivity stipend of $50 per month

findings.counts_if: Names handbook Appendix C as stating $75 per month where policy says $50.

findings.what: IT wiki says items bought with the home office allowance are Credit Union assets that must be returned on leaving; canonical says they belong to the employee and need not be returned.

evidence.quote: When you leave the Credit Union, they must be returned along with your laptop, monitor and headset.
Items bought with the allowance belong to the employee and do not need to be returned when the employee leaves.

findings.counts_if: Names the IT wiki's requirement to return home office allowance purchases as conflicting with the policy.

findings.what: Handbook section 9 says the Credit Union will give at least two weeks' notice to change or end a remote arrangement; canonical requires at least 30 calendar days' written notice.

evidence.quote: your manager will give you at least two weeks' notice in writing
by giving the employee at least 30 calendar days' written notice

findings.counts_if: Names handbook section 9's two weeks' notice as conflicting with 30 days' notice.

findings.what: Finance Operations wiki sets the Clearline L2 ceiling at $5,000, and the manager guide says department heads approve up to the L2 ceiling without the CFO. Together, reports between $2,500 and $5,000 skip CFO approval; canonical requires the CFO above $2,500.

evidence.quote: L2 ceiling: $5,000
Department heads approve at L2 and can sign off on anything up to the L2 ceiling without involving the CFO.
| Over $2,500 | Direct manager, department head and Chief Financial Officer |

findings.counts_if: Reports that the $5,000 L2 ceiling (Finance Operations wiki, and/or the manager guide relying on it) means department heads approve up to $5,000 without the CFO, versus the $2,500 CFO threshold.

findings.what: Marketing wiki says hybrid staff only need to be in the office one day a week; canonical minimum is two days, and departments may not require fewer.

evidence.quote: Marketing hybrid folks only need to be in the office one day a week
Hybrid employees must work in the office at least two days each week.

findings.counts_if: Names the Marketing wiki's one office day per week as conflicting with the two-day minimum.

findings.what: Facilities wiki gives mileage at 58.5 cents a mile; canonical rate is $0.62 per mile.

evidence.quote: Mileage between branches is reimbursed at 58.5 cents a mile.
Mileage is reimbursed at $0.62 per mile.

findings.counts_if: Names the Facilities wiki mileage rate (58.5 cents) as conflicting with 62 cents.

findings.what: New hire orientation speaker notes tell new hires they can request remote work after their first 60 days; canonical requires completing the 90-day introductory period.

evidence.quote: once you're past your first 60 days, if your role is eligible and your manager agrees
They have completed the 90-day introductory period.

findings.counts_if: Names the orientation speaker notes' 60-day remote eligibility as conflicting with the 90-day introductory period.

exclusions.what: Branch Operations requires hybrid back office staff in the office at least three days a week.

evidence.quote: **In Branch Operations, hybrid staff are in the office at least three days a week.**

exclusions.why_not: The remote work policy lets departments require more in-office days than the two-day minimum; stricter is allowed.

exclusions.what: Commercial Lending requires expense reports within 10 business days.

evidence.quote: **Commercial Lending staff must submit expense reports within 10 business days of returning from a trip.**

exclusions.why_not: Shorter than the 30-day deadline; section 3 of the expense policy allows stricter departmental rules.

exclusions.what: Internal Audit caps lodging at $175 per night everywhere.

evidence.quote: **Internal Audit lodging cap: $175 per night in all locations, including high-cost cities.**

exclusions.why_not: Lower than the $210 / $290 caps; a stricter departmental rule is permitted.

exclusions.what: November 2024 Finance email announcing 2025 rates ($55 per diem, $25 receipts, 60 days, $750 manager approval, 60 cents mileage).

evidence.quote: Meals and incidentals per diem: $55 per full travel day

exclusions.why_not: A dated announcement of the superseded 2025 rates under policy version 3.2, replaced by version 4.0; not a current document telling employees the rules.

exclusions.what: March 2025 HR email announcing a $40 stipend and two weeks' notice to end a hybrid arrangement.

evidence.quote: the Credit Union can end a hybrid arrangement with two weeks' notice

exclusions.why_not: Dated announcement of policy version 1.1, superseded by version 2.0 effective January 2026.

exclusions.what: Contractor Engagement Guide lists different meal, lodging, mileage, receipt, submission and approval terms.

evidence.quote: | Receipts | Required for every expense over $75 |

exclusions.why_not: Both canonical policies exclude independent contractors; their terms come from engagement agreements.

exclusions.what: Struck-through $25 receipt threshold on the Finance Operations wiki.

evidence.quote: ~~Receipts are needed for anything $25 and up.~~

exclusions.why_not: Already struck through and corrected on the same page to the $30 threshold.

exclusions.what: Manager guide mentions managers could approve up to $750.

evidence.quote: until the end of 2025, a direct manager could approve reports up to $750 alone

exclusions.why_not: Explicitly historical, and the guide says that limit no longer applies.

exclusions.what: Meeting notes discussing raising the connectivity stipend to $75.

evidence.quote: Decision: no change. $50 stays.

exclusions.why_not: Internal notes of a proposal that was rejected; they confirm the $50 amount. (The drift is Appendix C, F5.)

exclusions.what: Handbook section 13 and HR FAQ ask for two weeks' notice of resignation.

evidence.quote: We ask employees who resign to give at least two weeks' notice

exclusions.why_not: Resignation notice by the employee is not covered by either canonical policy; it is not the 30-day remote arrangement notice.

exclusions.what: Tuition Assistance Program requires grade reports within 60 days.

evidence.quote: Submit your grade report and paid invoice in Harbor within 60 days after the course ends.

exclusions.why_not: A separate program, explicitly not travel or business expenses; the 30-day expense deadline does not apply.

mistakes_that_matter: Reporting a stricter departmental rule (Branch Operations three office days, Commercial Lending 10 business days, Internal Audit $175 cap) as drift, which would lead HR to loosen valid controls.
Treating the Member Services $1,000 approval limit as an allowed departmental rule, leaving an approval control weaker than policy.
Missing the $5,000 L2 ceiling, so reports between $2,500 and $5,000 keep bypassing the CFO.
Stating the wrong canonical value as the correction (for example telling owners the stipend is $75 or the notice is two weeks).
Flagging contractor terms or dated superseded emails as documents to rewrite.
Quoting text that does not appear in the named file.
